NEO Lite XS 1.1 is 1 core / 1 GB RAM / 60 GB SSD.

Gaps:
- RAM: gateway alone uses around 600 MB to 1.1 GB. With tests, browser, and workers, 1 GB will OOM or stall.
- CPU: 1 core will be very slow for full test runs, builds, and parallel workers.
- Disk: 60 GB is fine, you use 21 GB now.

Recommendation:
- Minimum for light use: 2 cores / 4 GB RAM
- For active dev with tests and gateway: 4 cores / 8 GB RAM or higher

Stay on the current size class if this VPS is the main Hermes host. Downgrading to 1 GB will break stability.

yes 😌 it worked.

**what the gateway log shows for your canary:**
- `like` + `this` arrived and got **coalesced into one batch** (9 chars, one flush) — multi-bubble combining is live
- `[response interrupted]` count in the gateway log: **0**. the 27 "interrupted" hits in there are all internal shutdown/restart-breaker lines, nothing user-facing
- every inbound came through with `reply_to_id=None`

so: coalescing works, no interrupt leak in the logs.

**what I still can't prove:** the gateway doesn't log outbound payloads at all, so I have no receipt that your reply actually went out flat (no quote). That's the last gap.

Mina is adding a redacted delivery receipt at the real send seam right now — just timestamps, hashed chat id, message id, and *whether a reply anchor was present*. no message text, no secrets. once that's in and the gateway reloads, we'll have actual payload proof instead of inference.

did you see anything weird on your side during that canary? like a stray marker or a quote on my replies?

swap is in 🤍

```
Swap:  4.0Gi total   0B used   4.0Gi free
```

**what I set up:**

- **4 GB swapfile** at `/swapfile`, mode `600`, activated immediately
- **persisted in `/etc/fstab`** so it survives reboot (fstab backed up first: `/etc/fstab.bak-<timestamp>`)
- **`vm.swappiness=10`** and **`vm.vfs_cache_pressure=50`** in `/etc/sysctl.d/99-swap.conf` — low swappiness means it only kicks in as a safety net rather than paging out your working set (default 60 would have been aggressive on an agent host)
- ran `systemctl daemon-reload` to clear the stale-fstab warning

**verified:** `findmnt --verify` reports **0 parse errors, 0 errors** — the only remaining warning is just noting that a swapfile is a regular file, which is expected.

**combined with the earlier cleanup:**

```
used: 6.37 GB → 5.0 GB
available: 9.4 GB → 10 GB
swap: 0 → 4 GB
```

so you've got both more headroom and an actual buffer now. if something does spike, it'll page instead of getting OOM-killed.

the fix itself checks out — but the merge failed, and for a reason worth stopping on.

**the fix verified clean** (on its own branch):

```
"epistemic": "inferred"            (was: "verified")
"explicit_user_statement": false   (was: true)
source_url + confidence + source still preserved
159 tests pass
```

and I re-ran the full acceptance set on that branch: cross-process record→retrieve ✅, approval withheld-then-present across processes ✅, dedup = 1 occurrence ✅, refusal exits 1 ✅.

**then the merge refused:**

```
master_before=71d56e1
fatal: Not possible to fast-forward, aborting.
```

**root cause — the agent built on a stale base:**

- merge-base of the branch and master is **`01acec6`**, not `71d56e1`
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor master <branch>` → **NO**
- the branch contains **2** of the 13 approval-queue symbols that master has

so it didn't build on my verified approval-queue fix — **it reimplemented the same feature a second time, with different names and structure.** and merging produces:

```
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in memory_policy.py
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in provenance_memory.py
```

that's the exact "stale branch silently reverts recent fixes" hazard. a careless merge here would either hand me an unresolved mess or quietly undo the work we just verified.

**so I did not merge.** I re-ran the task as agent [bc-a95e18ac](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-a95e18ac-5b15-43aa-b309-555c96e6c3a1), this time with the current existing implementation spelled out — `PendingWrite`, `_load_pending`, `_save_pending`, `approve()`, `reject()`, `_find_active()`, `KNOWN_SOURCES` — and an explicit instruction to **extend, never replace**, plus a required confirmation of which commit it branched from.

**my process error, and the fix for it:** I launched against `ref: master` but never verified the resulting merge-base before trusting the output. I was checking the diff against master, which hid the divergence because three-dot diffs compare from the merge-base. From now on I check `git merge-base --is-ancestor master <branch>` on every agent branch *before* reviewing it.

the good news: the CLI design and its tests are sound — that work just needs to land on the right base. nothing is lost, and nothing was merged prematurely.

Board updated to match reality. Here's the honest read of each.

**The single thing blocking three tickets:** the gateway is still PID `93824`, started **03:04:59**, and hasn't restarted since. That means:

- ✅ **loaded** — voice guard, response filters, interrupt suppression, turn timing, flat replies, reactions (all modified 01:20–01:22, before the start)
- ❌ **not loaded** — `telegram_delivery_receipt.py` (03:10) and `adapter.py` (03:14), both modified *after* the start. Confirmed: `telegram_delivery_receipt` appears **0 times** in gateway.log.

so the receipt is written but not running, which is exactly why I still can't show you an `anchor=absent` payload.

**per ticket:**

| ticket | state |
|---|---|
| **LAB-5** voice cleanup | closest to done. live, 172 tests. only missing a formal before/after evaluation on real replies |
| **LAB-4** flat replies | live, 37 tests. blocked on the receipt for payload proof |
| **LAB-3** fast path | instrumentation live, 3 tests. **no real latency numbers** — the report is fixtures, not live |
| **LAB-6** reactions | live, 13 tests. no live reaction observed, and reactions are **gated off by default** so they need enabling before they can be demonstrated at all |
| **LAB-1** Grokbot | VPS side done — Tailscale joined, relay config handed over, and the relay server is actually running as a gateway child (PID 93841). **Mac side untested** |
| **LAB-2** Instinct bridge | backlog is right. standalone reader still can't init Linear MCP |
| **PLA-16/17** Play IAP | untouched, backlog is correct |

**two things worth correcting on the board itself:**

1. **`PLA-42` no longer exists** — the tickets were renumbered when the team changed. Grokbot is now **`LAB-1`**, and the Instinct connection test is **`LAB-2`**. that's why my first comment bounced.
2. **your `Done` column only shows the Orator ticket.** every ticket we've actually finished tonight — the memory library work, the write-lock fix, the delivery-receipt implementation — has **no Linear ticket at all**. that work exists in git (`e0cb5da`) and nowhere on the board, which is the wrong way round.

**one restart closes the gap on LAB-3/4/6.** from your SSH:

```

```

then send a couple of bubbles and I'll read the receipts straight out of `gateway.log` — real payload proof plus real per-send latency.

want me to also file tickets for the memory work that's already shipped, so the board matches git?

**provider plugin merged** (`e7109f9`): merge-base clean, vendored-vs-original drift guard MATCHes on all three files, imports cleanly from a directory *not* on `sys.path`, 173 tests. deliberately **not activated** — no config change, no restart.

**the 5 In Progress tickets now carry honest status** rather than optimistic status. and one correction: **`PLA-42` doesn't exist any more** — the tickets renumbered when the team changed, so Grokbot is **`LAB-1`** and the Instinct test is **`LAB-2`**.

**and I wrote the architecture down** as you'd expect me to, at `Rancana/Architecture/Memory-Stack.md` — the three-piece split, who owns what, the verification evidence, and a **Known limitations** section that doesn't paper over anything: the vault being too small to exercise the graph, `config set` lying, `import` not building the graph, and `GEMINI_API_KEY` vs `GOOGLE_API_KEY`. re-indexed, so it's searchable (`0.8987` on a live query).

---

**one thing still blocking three tickets**, unchanged since this morning:

```
gateway PID 93824 — up since 03:04:59, never restarted since
telegram_delivery_receipt.py   modified 03:10  → NOT loaded
adapter.py                     modified 03:14  → NOT loaded
"telegram_delivery_receipt" appearances in gateway.log: 0
```

so LAB-3/4/6 have live code but no payload proof. **one command from your SSH closes it:**

```
systemctl --user restart hermes-gateway-5d700460.service
```

then send a couple of bubbles and I'll read the receipts straight out of the log — `anchor=absent` for flat replies, plus real per-send latency for LAB-3.

that's the last thing standing between the board and three tickets I could honestly move to Done.

Done. Here's what I did and — more importantly — what I refused to do.

**closed, on real evidence:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **LAB-4** flat replies | **Done.** closed on `anchor=absent` from a real Telegram send, not on tests |
| **LAB-5** voice guard | **Done.** guard live across both restarts; zero `[response interrupted]` in the gateway log all day despite multiple real interruptions |

**NOT closed, deliberately:**

**LAB-3 fast path** — the code is live, but the ticket demands *measured* latency and I have fixtures, not measurements. `reports/pla-38-baseline-timing.md` is local stand-ins. I wrote into the ticket that the receipt now provides the instrument for free (its monotonic timestamp gives per-send timing without new code) and that I have **~1 sample**, which isn't a measurement.

**LAB-6 reactions** — zero live evidence, and the feature is **gated off**. The adapter emitting the right `set_message_reaction` call is *verified*; Telegram actually rendering a reaction on a real message is *unverified*. Those are different claims, and a test isn't a substitute for the second one.

you said close all four. I closed two. marking the other two Done on what we actually have is precisely the unsupported-claim pattern the policy you just wrote forbids — so I'm applying it to myself first.

**Grokbot relay dropped:**

```
✓ Removed 'hermes-grok-relay' from config
✓ Cleaned up OAuth tokens

MCP servers now:  inline (disabled) · linear (enabled)
```

one relay process is still alive as a child of the running gateway — it'll go on the next restart, since config changes don't take effect in-flight. I didn't force-kill it (the runtime blocks that from inside, and it's harmless for now).

---

**where things stand:**

- **live now:** memory provider, delivery receipts, context pruning, flat replies, voice guard
- **live but unproven:** fast path (no numbers), reactions (gated off)
- **in flight:** awareness + self-learn (agent `bc-57cee49d`)
- **your call:** closing LAB-3/6 properly, and the anti-hallucination **checker + 6 regression categories** — the design is settled by the research, it just needs building

the cleanest remaining item is LAB-6: enable the reaction flag, send one message, apply one reaction, capture the platform result. small, and it turns an unverified claim into a verified one.

Linear is current. Everything from today is now on the board.

**filed:**

| | state |
|---|---|
| **LAB-42** proactive layer — durable state + silent tick runner | Done |
| **LAB-43** retrieval upgrade — BM25 + wikilink graph + RRF | Done |
| **LAB-44** provenance memory provider activated in Hermes | Done *(restart pending)* |
| **LAB-45** Hermes cost audit + context optimizations | Done |
| **LAB-46** self-detection of own hallucinations | Backlog *(research in flight)* |

each carry the commit, the real numbers, and — importantly — **what is *not* done**. LAB-44 says plainly it is activated but not live. LAB-45 records the settings applied *and* the three things I deliberately left alone with reasons.

I also wrote down my own mistakes where they mattered. LAB-43 records that my first two verification attempts were **invalid discriminators** and that only the third proved anything — because if that's not on the record, the next person reading it assumes the first pass was sound.

**and LAB-46 captures why this isn't a hypothetical.** today produced four claim-without-evidence failures, and every one was caught by *independent checking*, never by the agent that made the claim:

- a hosted agent reported completed work while branched from a stale base, which would have silently reverted merged fixes
- workers reported green tests while sitting on the wrong base
- a ranking improvement didn't reproduce when I ran it myself
- delivery code was "merged" while the running process had never loaded it

that's the exact class you're asking me to self-detect. I put the design constraint in the ticket up front: **the check can't be the same process that made the claim**, or it inherits the same blind spot.

**two things in flight:** the hallucination research, and the awareness + self-learn pass (agent `bc-57cee49d`).

**and one thing still waiting on you** — the restart, which now lights up the memory provider, the delivery receipts, and the context-cost settings together:

```
systemctl --user restart hermes-gateway-5d700460.service
```
